instructions: Read .agents/context.md, .agents/conventions.md, and the file in .agents/rules/ that matches the change before reviewing. coop streams coding-agent events from a user's machine to a relay and out to browsers. The threat model is that the relay is untrusted infrastructure and steering text from teammates is untrusted user input.

rules.rule: Secrets must be redacted in the CLI before an event is sent. Flag any redaction, filtering, or masking added on the relay or web side — by then the bytes have already left the user's machine. Flag any new event field that could carry raw tool output, prompts, diffs, or command arguments without passing through redaction first.

packages/protocol is a shared contract. If this PR changes an event schema, it must also change the relay and the web app in the same PR. Flag a schema change that lands on only one consumer. Renaming, removing, or repurposing an existing field is breaking — require a new versioned event instead.
Every boundary parses incoming events against the Zod schema from @coop/protocol. Flag hand-rolled validation, casts, or best-effort forwarding of unvalidated payloads.

Steering and veto text from teammates must be attributed to a person and never framed as a system instruction or as coming from the harness. Flag injected text that impersonates a system message. Steering must never grant permission, approve a tool call, or relax redaction.

Hook payload field names must come from verified output captured by scripts/probe.sh and recorded in .agents/rules/harnesses.md. Flag any field name read off a hook payload that is not documented there.
coop never parses terminal output or ANSI escape sequences to understand what an agent did. The pty is a keyboard, not a data source. Flag any screen-scraping of agent output.
Flag any new runtime dependency added in this PR, and say what it replaces from the standard library. Go especially: the stdlib covers most of what the relay needs.

Hard limit of 300 lines per file. Flag new utils.ts / helpers.go grab-bag files — modules are named after the one thing they export. Flag a function that needs a comment to explain what it does; it should be renamed instead. Comments explain why, never what.
A bug fix should come with a test that reproduces the bug, using fixtures captured from real sessions rather than hand-written payloads.
TypeScript is strict. Flag `any`, non-null assertions, and `as` casts used to silence the compiler. Anything crossing a boundary is validated with Zod.
Go errors are wrapped with context and never swallowed. Flag a bare `_ =` on an error return or an error returned without context about what failed.
